speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing agitation and yellowing of your skin and eyes; have you noticed any recent changes in your urine color or stool consistency? Also, have you experienced nausea, vomiting, or confusion lately?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of high-risk behaviors and recent agitation, have you noticed any painful urination, fever, or new rashes? Also, when was your last sexual contact, and have you been taking any new medications or supplements?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Appendicitis. The patient's history of yellow skin and eyes is likely unrelated to his primary surgical issue, but his current presentation of agitation and severe pain is classic for appendicitis, which can cause systemic agitation if perforation or sepsis is developing. I will proceed with an immediate surgical consultation and CT scan of the abdomen to confirm the diagnosis.
